title: Saving & Managing Projects 📁
description: Keep your work safe and understand the project structure.

slides.title: Saving Your Level 💾
slides.content:
# Don't Lose Progress!

Unreal Engine uses a **level** system. Each level (map) is a separate file.

* **Ctrl + S** – save current level
* **File → Save All** – save all dirty assets (modified but unsaved)
* **Unsaved assets** show an asterisk `*` next to their name

**Important:** Saving the level does **not** automatically save asset changes (e.g., material edits). Use **Save All** regularly.

*Analogy:* Think of a level as a **document**, and assets as **images** inside it. Each must be saved separately.

quizData.question: Saving the level automatically saves all asset changes.
quizData.explanation: Level files and asset files are saved independently. Use Save All to save everything.

slides.title: Project Folder Structure 📂
slides.content:
## What’s Inside Your Project?

Navigate to your project folder in Windows Explorer to see:

* **Config** – project settings files
* **Content** – ALL your assets (materials, blueprints, levels)
* **Intermediate** – temporary build files (don’t touch)
* **Saved** – logs, screenshots, auto‑saves

**Content** is your workspace – you’ll spend 90% of your time here. It mirrors the Content Browser.

slides.title: Backup Reminder ⚠️
slides.content:
## Protect Your Work

* Use **Source Control** (Git, Perforce) when possible
* At minimum, periodically copy the entire project folder to an external drive
* The **Saved** folder contains auto‑saves that can rescue you from crashes

quizData.question: Which folder contains all your game assets like materials and blueprints?
quizData.explanation: The Content folder holds all project assets. Intermediate and Saved are for temporary/build files.
